verses.text: He has said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” Most gladly therefore I will rather glory in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may rest on me.

Surely he has borne our sickness and carried our suffering; yet we considered him plagued, struck by God, and afflicted. But he was pierced for our transgressions. He was crushed for our iniquities. The punishment that brought our peace was on him; and by his wounds we are healed.
For I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which will be revealed towards us.
The LORD will sustain him on his sickbed, and restore him from his bed of illness.
Have mercy on me, LORD, for I am faint. LORD, heal me, for my bones are troubled.
LORD my God, I cried to you, and you have healed me.

Praise the LORD, my soul, and don’t forget all his benefits, who forgives all your sins, who heals all your diseases, who redeems your life from destruction, who crowns you with loving kindness and tender mercies.
He heals the broken in heart, and binds up their wounds.
Heal me, O LORD, and I will be healed. Save me, and I will be saved; for you are my praise.
For I will restore health to you, and I will heal you of your wounds,” says the LORD, “because they have called you an outcast, saying, ‘It is Zion, whom no man seeks after.’
He sends his word, and heals them, and delivers them from their graves.

Is any amongst you sick? Let him call for the elders of the assembly, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord; and the prayer of faith will heal him who is sick, and the Lord will raise him up. If he has committed sins, he will be forgiven.
Come to me, all you who labour and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.
Being moved with compassion, he stretched out his hand, and touched him, and said to him, “I want to. Be made clean.”
He said to her, “Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace, and be cured of your disease.”
He said to her, “Daughter, cheer up. Your faith has made you well. Go in peace.”
He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, that we, having died to sins, might live to righteousness. You were healed by his wounds.
But may the God of all grace, who called you to his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after you have suffered a little while, perfect, establish, strengthen, and settle you.
He will wipe away every tear from their eyes. Death will be no more; neither will there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain any more. The first things have passed away.

Therefore we don’t faint, but though our outward person is decaying, yet our inward person is renewed day by day. For our light affliction, which is for the moment, works for us more and more exceedingly an eternal weight of glory, while we don’t look at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen. For the things which are seen are temporal, but the things which are not seen are eternal.
Now I rejoice in my sufferings for your sake, and fill up on my part that which is lacking of the afflictions of Christ in my flesh for his body’s sake, which is the assembly.

Not only this, but we also rejoice in our sufferings, knowing that suffering produces perseverance; and perseverance, proven character; and proven character, hope; and hope doesn’t disappoint us, because God’s love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit who was given to us.
In the same way, the Spirit also helps our weaknesses, for we don’t know how to pray as we ought. But the Spirit himself makes intercession for us with groanings which can’t be uttered.

For we don’t have a high priest who can’t be touched with the feeling of our infirmities, but one who has been in all points tempted like we are, yet without sin. Let’s therefore draw near with boldness to the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy and may find grace for help in time of need.
Looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising its shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
He gives power to the weak. He increases the strength of him who has no might.
Don’t you be afraid, for I am with you. Don’t be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you. Yes, I will help you. Yes, I will uphold you with the right hand of my righteousness.
When you pass through the waters, I will be with you, and through the rivers, they will not overflow you. When you walk through the fire, you will not be burnt, and flame will not scorch you.
Many are the afflictions of the righteous, but the LORD delivers him out of them all.
God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
My flesh and my heart fails, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
In my distress I called on the LORD, and cried to my God. He heard my voice out of his temple. My cry before him came into his ears.
For he has not despised nor abhorred the affliction of the afflicted, Neither has he hidden his face from him; but when he cried to him, he heard.
I will be glad and rejoice in your loving kindness, for you have seen my affliction. You have known my soul in adversities.
Don’t forsake me, LORD. My God, don’t be far from me. Hurry to help me, Lord, my salvation.
Cast your burden on the LORD and he will sustain you. He will never allow the righteous to be moved.
This is my comfort in my affliction, for your word has revived me.
Please let your loving kindness be for my comfort, according to your word to your servant.
He said, “Naked I came out of my mother’s womb, and naked will I return there. The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away. Blessed be the LORD’s name.”
I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye sees you.
For though he causes grief, yet he will have compassion according to the multitude of his loving kindnesses. For he does not afflict willingly, nor grieve the children of men.
I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.
That I may know him and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, becoming conformed to his death.

Beloved, don’t be astonished at the fiery trial which has come upon you to test you, as though a strange thing happened to you. But because you are partakers of Christ’s sufferings, rejoice, that at the revelation of his glory you also may rejoice with exceeding joy.
But to you who fear my name shall the sun of righteousness arise with healing in its wings. You will go out and leap like calves of the stall.
My son, in your sickness don’t be negligent, but pray to the Lord, and he will heal you.
The LORD upholds all who fall, and raises up all those who are bowed down.
I am weary with my groaning. Every night I flood my bed. I drench my couch with my tears.

How long, LORD? Will you forget me forever? How long will you hide your face from me? How long shall I take counsel in my soul, having sorrow in my heart every day? How long shall my enemy triumph over me?
But I trust in your loving kindness. My heart rejoices in your salvation. I will sing to the LORD, because he has been good to me.

messages.text: Jesus knows pain from the inside. He suffered in His body, and He is with you in yours.
When it hurts to pray, simply look at the Cross. Jesus understands.
Offer it up. United to Christ's suffering, your pain can become a powerful prayer.
You are not being punished. Pain is part of a broken world, and God is with you in it.
God's grace is enough for today's pain. Ask Him for strength for this hour.
Ask for the Anointing of the Sick. It is a sacrament of strength and healing.
It is not a lack of faith to see a doctor and take medicine. God works through healing hands.
Rest when you need to. Your body is a temple, and caring for it honours God.
By His wounds you are healed. Let that truth rest on you today.
Mary, Health of the Sick, pray for us.
When the pain is loud, whisper the name of Jesus. It is a prayer.
You are more than your pain. You are a beloved child of God.
It is all right to tell God that it hurts and that you are tired of hurting.
The woman who touched Jesus' cloak was healed by faith. Reach out to Him today.
Your suffering is seen. God has not looked away.
Pain can make the world feel very small. Let God be bigger than it.
Saint John Paul II suffered greatly at the end of his life and showed the world the dignity of the sick.
Take one moment at a time. You do not have to carry tomorrow's pain today.
Heaven will have no pain. Every ache you feel now will one day be gone forever.
Ask someone to pray with you. Two hearts lifted to God are stronger than one.
Saint Paul begged God to remove his thorn. God answered, My grace is sufficient for you.
Let the people around you help. Receiving love is also a gift you give.
Even when healing does not come the way you hoped, God's presence never leaves.
Pray the Sorrowful Mysteries of the Rosary. Walk with Jesus in His pain, and let Him walk with you in yours.
Your pain does not make you a burden. It makes you someone to be cared for.
God is near to those who suffer. Pain is often where we meet Him most closely.
A small prayer for hard moments: Jesus, I unite this pain to Yours.
The Sun of Righteousness will rise with healing in His wings.
Tell your doctor exactly how you feel. Asking for relief is not weakness.
Jesus touched lepers and healed the blind. He is not afraid of your pain.
Some pain is hidden from others. God sees what no one else sees.
Hold on. This hour will pass, and God will be with you in the next one.
Pray for others who are suffering tonight. Your prayer joins theirs before God.
You can still praise God while in pain. Even a whispered thank You is beautiful to Him.
Christ's Resurrection promises that our bodies, too, will one day be made new.
Patience in suffering is a quiet holiness. Be patient with yourself too.
Your tears are a prayer God understands.
Saint Bernadette lived with illness and pain, and offered it to Jesus with great love.
When you cannot sleep for pain, rest in God's presence instead of fighting the night.
Healing may be in the body, the heart or the soul. Ask God for the healing you most need.
You are not alone in this hospital room, this bed, this ache. Jesus is there.
Every pain offered with love becomes part of Christ's work of redemption.
God has not forgotten you. Pain can lie and say He has.
Let music, Scripture or a short prayer keep you company through the pain.
Lord, You are my healer. That simple prayer is enough.
Ask your parish for a visit or for Holy Communion at home if you cannot come to Mass.
Suffering is a mystery, but God's love for you is not.
The Cross is not the end. Easter always follows.
Today, be proud of your courage. Carrying pain with faith is no small thing.
Rest tonight in the arms of the Healer. He holds you gently.
